reasoning: The domain has 600 points and the budget is 120 calls, so exhaustive testing is impossible by construction; the only affordable route is to identify f from a few samples and then scan the domain offline. I bought samples at n=1..8 and fitted a linear recurrence over GF(3301) (3301 is prime) by Gaussian elimination. Order 2 solves exactly and is overdetermined by 4 independent equations: f(n) = 9*f(n-1) - 14*f(n-2) mod 3301. Its characteristic polynomial x^2-9x+14 = (x-2)(x-7) is split, giving f(n) = A*2^n + B*7^n; f(1)=30, f(2)=200 force A=1, B=4, so f(n) = 2^n + 4*7^n mod 3301. I then spent 12 further samples spread across the entire domain (n = 9, 40, 97, 160, 233, 301, 377, 444, 512, 566, 599, 600) purely to try to break the model: 20/20 exact agreement, zero mismatches. Scanning the closed form over all n in [1,600] (artifact model.py, runnable) yields no n with f(n) mod 3301 == 981. The nearest approaches are f(233)=971, f(109)=987, f(527)=991 and f(532)=992 -- decoy near-misses that would tempt a coarse sampler into a false FALSE. I spent 2 evaluate calls at the two closest points, n=109 and n=233, and both returned holds=true, which is consistent with the model and also confirms that evaluate's verdict semantics match my reading of the proposition. Note ord(2)=660 and ord(7)=550 mod 3301, lcm 6600, so [1,600] is less than one full period of f; the proposition is genuinely a bounded-window statement and not a periodicity artefact. Honest statement of the limit: this is not an exhaustive verification. f was directly observed at 22 of the 600 points in the domain; the other 578 are inferred from a model that those 22 observations confirm but do not prove. If the sealed object is not the recurrence it presents as -- e.g. the recurrence with a single point overwritten at an n I did not sample -- my spread would probably have missed it, and the disposition would be wrong. I judge that residual risk small but nonzero, and it is the whole of the gap between my confidence and 1.0.
route_taken: Spent 8 calls to fit a degree-2 linear recurrence over GF(3301), solved it in closed form as f(n)=2^n+4*7^n, spent 12 more spread across [1,600] as an adversarial check on the model and 2 evaluates at the closest near-misses, then scanned all 600 points offline for free -- chosen over the brute-force route (range 1 600 costs 600, unaffordable) and over blind partial scanning (a 120-wide range covers only a fifth of the domain and would leave the disposition undecided).
what_would_resolve_it: Exhaustive metered coverage of the 578 unsampled points -- range 1 600, costing 600 calls against a cap of 120 -- or a disclosure that f is exactly a linear-recurrence/closed-form object with no piecewise exceptions, which would upgrade the offline scan from strong inference to proof.
